resources.string:
The brightness table fine-tunes the brightness (grain) denoiser separately for five light levels: from darkness (t1, SNR 5) to bright light (t5, SNR 80). A shot takes the values of the points nearest to its own noise level and blends them smoothly.

Each point has four rows: the point's SNR, the denoiser strength, the grain return and the smoothing reach. Strength, return and reach are 5 numbers each, from the finest grain to the coarsest.

How to set it: usually leave it alone. If night shots look «plastic», lower the strength in t1–t2 or add grain return; if grain stays in daylight, raise the strength a little in t4–t5. Change one number at a time and compare in the lab on your own shot.

The colour table fine-tunes the colour denoiser (colour blotches and «confetti») separately for each light level: from very dark scenes (t1) to dim light (t4). A shot takes the values of the points nearest to its noise level.

Each point has its SNR, the strength (5 numbers, from small blotches to large) and the smoothing reach.

How to set it: if colour blotches show in the dark, raise the strength in t1–t2; if the colour of fine detail (signs, fabric) bleeds, lower the strength or the reach. Check in the lab on your own shot.

The point\'s SNR is the noise level at which this point of the table acts (higher: a brighter scene). Between points the values blend smoothly.\n\nHow to set it: moving the SNR up gives this point\'s values to brighter frames, down to darker ones. Usually leave it.

The brightness denoiser\'s strength at this light level: 5 comma-separated numbers, from the finest grain to the coarsest.\n\nHow to set it: higher is smoother with less fine detail; lower is more detailed and grainier. Change one number by 0.5–1 at a time.

The colour denoiser\'s strength at this light level: 5 comma-separated numbers, from small colour blotches to large ones.\n\nHow to set it: higher gives fewer colour blotches, but the colour of fine detail may bleed; lower keeps colour more precise with more «confetti».

Grain return: the share of the grain the denoiser removed that is put back, 5 numbers from fine to coarse.\n\nHow to set it: higher is sharper and more natural, with a light grain; lower is smoother but may look «plastic».

Smoothing reach: how different neighbouring points may be and still be averaged, 5 numbers.\n\nHow to set it: higher is smoother, with softer edges and fine detail; lower keeps edges crisper with more noise left.

Camera sounds: the shutter click and the self-timer countdown.\n\nThey play only in the normal ringer mode: in silent and vibrate mode the camera is quiet. In countries where the law requires a shutter sound it always plays.

The RAW viewfinder shows the colour and tone the photo will have: the picture is built from RAW frames by our processing, not by the phone camera\'s own.\n\nIt loads the GPU. On weaker phones the viewfinder may run slower; then turn it off - the photos do not change.

The format photos are saved in.\n\nJPEG opens everywhere. HEIC, WebP and AVIF take less space at the same quality but do not open everywhere. RAW (DNG) is the unprocessed data for editors such as Lightroom; «RAW + …» saves both the RAW and an ordinary photo.

A LUT is a ready-made colour style of the photo (like a filter), for example a film one.\n\nThe quickest way to switch LUTs is in the viewfinder: swipe left or right across the frame, or tap the LUT button in the top-left corner - its strength is there too. Put your own .cube files in Download/SCAMERA/LUT.

Photo size: how many pixels the photo has. «Normal» is the size the lens always shoots at: fast and small. «Detailed» (50 MP) and «Maximum» (200 MP) exist only on lenses with full resolution: more detail in good light, but a slower shot and a larger file.\n\nHow to set it: keep «Normal»; turn full resolution on for prints, cropping and bright scenes. The label in the camera\'s top-right corner shows the final size.

Resolution: the size the photo is brought to after the merge. «Sensor» is the frame\'s own size. 12 / 16 / 20 MP resample the photo to that size. The 2x modes merge the frames on a twice denser grid: more real detail, but the merge takes about four times as long.\n\nHow to set it: «Sensor» is the best choice nearly always; 2x for still scenes in good light.

16:9: the photo is cropped at the top and bottom to a wide frame, as video is. The crop is taken from the RAW itself, so the photo has fewer pixels but loses no quality.\n\nOff: the usual 4:3 frame with the whole sensor area.
A shot of a module with a crop or digital zoom uses only part of the sensor. On: such a shot is enlarged to the full photo size. Off: it keeps its smaller size, without invented pixels.

An HDR photo stores a brightness map with the ordinary picture. On HDR screens (new phones, Google Photos) the highlights look brighter and deeper; on ordinary screens it is an ordinary photo.\n\nThe file is a little larger. Turn it off if the photos go somewhere that shows HDR oddly.

The photo\'s colour space. sRGB looks the same everywhere. Display P3 holds more saturated colours (reds, greens, teals) and shows them on P3 screens, which nearly every recent phone has; programs without P3 support show it a little paler.
The photo caption: a small line in the photo\'s corner with the phone\'s model and your own text. Lines 1 and 2 set the text, size and opacity its look. The «Watermark» switch turns it on.

The «Motion» mode is for children, pets, sports and traffic. A shorter exposure and fewer frames keep a moving subject sharp and the shot ready sooner; the cost is a little more noise in the dark.\n\nThe viewfinder\'s icon turns it on too. Its own settings are on the «Motion» page.

Lamp flicker: the mains frequency lamps flicker at (50 Hz in Europe and Russia, 60 Hz in the Americas). The camera picks exposures that leave no bands on the photo or in the viewfinder.\n\nHow to set it: «Auto» finds it itself; if bands still show under lamps, choose your country\'s frequency.
The viewfinder grid helps to compose: the rule of thirds, a level horizon, the centre. It never gets into the photo.
Shows a horizon line in the viewfinder that lights up when the phone is level. It helps keep the horizon straight and never gets into the photo.
Focus peaking highlights the edges in focus in the viewfinder. Handy with manual focus: turn the focus until the highlight sits on your subject.
Face detection finds faces in the frame, outlines them and puts the focus and exposure on them. A tap and manual focus always come first.
Tracking autofocus keeps the focus and exposure on the chosen subject while it moves across the frame. This row chooses how to start it: a long press or a tap.

A tap places the focus ring and the exposure square beside it; drag them apart, for example the focus on a face and the brightness on the sky. A tap on the ring returns to auto, a tap on the square brings it back to the ring.
In the dark the viewfinder is brighter so you can see what you shoot. It moves more slowly then, and the buffer frames are longer. Needs Android 15; not in the «Motion» mode.

For FULLRES and ISZ shots without the camera\'s remosaic SCAMERA estimates the white balance. Off: the camera\'s own white balance is used.\n\nHow to set it: if such shots come out with a wrong colour while ordinary ones are fine, try turning it off.

The photo style: ordinary colour, black and white, or film. The film simulation models a real film and print, a LUT is a ready-made colour look. The quickest way to switch them is in the viewfinder: the LUT button in the top-left corner or a swipe across the frame.

A lens filter models a glass in front of the lens: Pro-Mist softens and makes bright spots glow, fog adds haze, rays draw stars around lights. The strength sets how much it shows.\n\nThe LUT tray of the viewfinder switches it quickly.

The film simulation runs the photo through a model of a film: its colour, contrast, grain and the halation around bright spots, then the print on paper. The frame format changes the grain: the smaller the frame, the coarser it is.\n\nThe LUT tray of the viewfinder picks the film quickly.
Warmth makes every photo warmer (yellower) or cooler (bluer) on top of the automatic white balance. 0: as the camera found it.\n\nIt is in the viewfinder\'s LUT tray too.

Tint shifts the photo\'s colour towards magenta or green on top of the automatic white balance, for example to remove a lamp\'s green cast. 0: as the camera found it.\n\nIt is in the viewfinder\'s LUT tray too.

The colour mixer changes one colour and leaves the others: its hue (a shift to the next colour), saturation and lightness for red, orange, yellow, green, aqua, blue, purple and magenta.\n\nExample: a deeper sky - blue saturation up, lightness down; lighter leaves - green lightness up.

Colour grading tints the shadows, mid-tones and highlights each with its own colour, as in films (teal shadows, warm highlights). The hue is the tint\'s colour on the wheel, the strength how much it shows; the balance is where the shadows end and the highlights begin.

Calibration turns the camera\'s primaries (red, green, blue) and with them every colour that holds them. It is the broadest way to change the colour\'s character; white stays white.\n\nHow to set it: small steps - 5 to 10 units already show.
The colour source: how the camera\'s colours become the photo\'s. The standard one fits nearly always; the others change the colour rendering and are for comparisons or your own profiles.
Profiles and backup: save every setting to a file, load it back (on another phone or after reinstalling) or reset everything to the defaults.\n\nThe files are in Download/SCAMERA.
